title: Dirichlet's Approximation Theorem via Minkowski: Axiom-Free Proof

problemStatement.formal: Prove Dirichlet approximation via Minkowski with no axioms by proving the Dirichlet parallelogram is open, convex, and has volume 4*(Q+1)/Q.
problemStatement.plain: Replace the earlier axiomatized geometric steps in the Minkowski proof of Dirichlet approximation with fully verified Mathlib arguments.
whyMatters: Turns an axiomatized geometry-of-numbers proof into an axiom-free proof
Gives a reusable pattern for eliminating measure and convexity assumptions

proven: The Dirichlet parallelogram is open and measurable.
Convexity follows from linear preimages of open intervals.
The shear-map volume calculation and final Dirichlet approximation theorem are proved with 0 axioms and 0 sorries.
open: Extend the method to simultaneous Dirichlet approximation.
Investigate Hurwitz and metric Diophantine approximation refinements.
knownResults.goal: Record the axiom-free replacement for the Minkowski proof of Dirichlet approximation.

currentState.focus: Verified source-backed record: primary proof has 267 lines, 7 public theorems plus 1 private theorem, 1 definition, 0 axioms, and 0 sorries.
currentState.nextAction: Optional follow-on: generalize the axiom-free argument to simultaneous approximation.

insights: Openness gives measurability cleanly through IsOpen.measurableSet.
Convexity is reduced to preimages of convex intervals under linear maps.
